newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders confirm Saudi barley deal, await details.
newsitem.headline: Traders confirm Saudi barley deal, await details.

text.p: Grain traders on Wednesday confirmed Saudi Arabia's purchase of 500,000 tonnes of world barley and said the market was now waiting for a breakdown of prices and the names of potential sellers.
"It's clear they have bought. That's confirmed," one trader involved in the Saudi purchase tender said.
Contrary to earlier indications, the trader said most companies had submitted offers at the tender dated April 8 for 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley in April and May.
But the list of firms in the running to secure contracts had not yet emerged, he and other European traders said.
Industry sources had said they believed only four companies were being actively considered, with some expressing concern about penalties for late delivery due to tight schedules.
The tender is for 100,000 tonnes in late April, 150,000 tonnes in first-half May and 250,000 tonnes in second-half May.
Latest estimates of purchase prices ranged between $150 and $152 per tonne, cost and freight, or $152 to 154 per tonne.
With freight taken off, traders valued these prices below $130 per tonne, fob Europe, perhaps as low as $127 per tonne.
Main potential suppliers included the European Union and -- said to be pushing actively to sell -- Canada. There was talk Turkey may be offering but this could not be confirmed.
Turkey cancelled its last export tender due to low bids, but would probably surface as a seller at some stage, traders said.
